note.explanation: The Network Layer transfers data between different networks and selects a path from source to destination. For example, it is like a GPS choosing a route from home to school. The Data Link Layer handles node-to-node transfer, while the Network Layer handles transfer between networks.
examples: A GPS finding a route is an example of the Network Layer choosing a path.
IP addresses help the Network Layer route data between networks.
note.checkAnswer: The Network Layer transfers data between different networks and determines the best path from source to destination.
note.simple: The Network Layer is like a GPS for data: it helps data travel between networks by choosing a path.

note.title: What does the Network Layer do?

note.answer: The Network Layer transfers data between different networks and determines the best path for data to travel from source to destination.

mcqs.stem: A computer sends data to a device on a different network. Which OSI layer is responsible for choosing the route?
rationales: The Physical Layer sends bits through a physical medium, not choosing routes.
The Data Link Layer handles node-to-node transfer and error detection.
The Network Layer selects a path and transfers data between different networks.
The Transport Layer manages data flow and error checking between processes.

mcqs.stem: Which OSI layer is at the bottom of the model?
rationales: Layer 1, the Physical Layer, is the bottom layer.
Layer 3 is the Network Layer, above the Data Link Layer.
Layer 5 is the Session Layer, near the top half of the model.
Layer 7, the Application Layer, is at the top.

mcqs.stem: Which OSI layer establishes, maintains, and terminates connections between devices?
rationales: The Data Link Layer handles node-to-node data transport and error detection.
The Transport Layer manages data transfer between processes, including flow control and error checking.
The Session Layer establishes, maintains, and terminates sessions between applications.
The Presentation Layer formats and encrypts data for the receiving system.

mcqs.stem: Which layer formats and encrypts data so that it is readable by the receiving system?
rationales: The Physical Layer focuses on sending bits through a physical medium.
The Network Layer routes data between different networks.
The Presentation Layer formats and encrypts data for the receiving system.
The Application Layer provides network services directly to applications.

mcqs.stem: A user uses email or a web browser to access network services. Which OSI layer is closest to the user?
rationales: The Application Layer is closest to the user and provides network services to applications.
The Data Link Layer handles node-to-node transfer and error detection.
The Physical Layer handles the physical connection and transmission of bits.
The Transport Layer manages data transfer between processes.

options: A router selecting the best path between networks

mcqs.stem: Which task is performed by the Network Layer?
rationales: A network cable is part of the physical connection handled by the Physical Layer.
Selecting a path between networks is the Network Layer's responsibility.
Ending a session is managed by the Session Layer.
Formatting data for the receiving system is handled by the Presentation Layer.

mcqs.stem: At which OSI layer does the textbook say TCP is used to help ensure reliable data transfer?
rationales: Layer 2 is the Data Link Layer, which handles node-to-node transfer.
Layer 4 is the Transport Layer, which uses protocols such as TCP for reliable data transfer.
Layer 6 is the Presentation Layer, which formats and encrypts data.
Layer 7 is the Application Layer, which provides services such as email and web browsing.

mcqs.stem: Which layer detects and corrects errors and handles node-to-node data transport?
rationales: The Data Link Layer handles error detection and correction, as well as node-to-node data transport.
The Session Layer manages sessions between applications.
The Transport Layer manages data flow and error checking between processes.
The Application Layer provides network services directly to applications.

explain.title: The OSI model has seven layers
explain.body: The Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) Model is a framework used to understand how different networking protocols interact. It has 7 layers, each with a specific function. From bottom to top, the layers are Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, and Application.

explain.title: Physical and Data Link layers
explain.body: The Physical Layer is liable for the actual connection between devices. The process of sending unprocessed data bits via a physical medium is the focus here. The Data Link Layer handles error detection and correction, as well as node-to-node data transport. It ensures error-free data transmission from the Physical Layer.

explain.title: Network and Transport layers
explain.body: The Network Layer is responsible for data transfer between different networks. It determines the best path for data to travel from the source to the destination. The Transport Layer ensures that data is transferred from one process rerunning on source end system to a process souring on destination end system. It manages data flow control and error checking.

explain.title: Session and Presentation layers
explain.body: The Session Layer manages sessions between applications. It establishes, maintains, and terminates connections between devices. The Presentation Layer translates data between the application layer and the network. It formats and encrypts data to ensure it is readable by the receiving system.

explain.title: Application layer
explain.body: The Application Layer is the closest to the end user. It provides network services directly to applications, such as email, web browsing, and file transfer.

mistakes: Mixing up the Network Layer, which routes data between networks, and the Data Link Layer, which handles node-to-node transfer.
Writing only that the Network Layer transfers data, but forgetting to mention that it determines the best path.
Reversing the order of the layers; Layer 1 is Physical and Layer 7 is Application.
Saying that the Transport Layer selects the route; route selection belongs to the Network Layer.
